The 4 levels of using AI at work How to use AI at work: there are four levels, and most people never leave level one. Chat. You paste something into ChatGPT or Claude, it answers, you copy it back out. Useful, but you're the delivery guy carrying every answer between your apps by hand. Context. Give it your price list, your process docs and ten emails you wrote so it learns how you sound. Same AI, completely different answers, because now it answers like it works at your company. Connected tools. Out of the box, AI can't open your CRM or read your spreadsheet. Almost every app has a door for other software called an API, and MCP is a standard plug that lets AI walk through those doors. Once it's connected, it sees your contacts, your sheets and your email, and it acts: update, send, create. Updating 2,000 customer records from last month's invoices is two weeks of somebody's life. Connected AI does it in minutes. Run it on ten records first, check them, then let it do the rest. Automations. Level three still needs you to ask. Level four starts on its own: a new lead comes in, an invoice lands, Monday at 8am. A tool like n8n moves the data between your apps, and the AI in the middle does the thinking: reads the email, picks the category, writes the reply. Your business keeps running while you sleep. The whole ladder: chat, context, connected tools, automations. On level three you talk and it does the work. On level four you don't even have to talk. Claude Duet: the Claude that comes to you first Anthropic just opened a research preview of Claude Duet, and it flips how you use Claude. The Claude you know waits for you to open a chat. Duet comes to you. Every morning it sends a short brief on what matters across your email, calendar and connected apps. Then it checks in every few hours and only messages you when something actually needs you. It runs on its own computer in the cloud, with its own browser, so it keeps working with your laptop closed. It brings your memory, skills and connectors from your Claude account. And before it sends a message, pays, signs or deletes anything, it shows you exactly what it's about to do and waits for your yes. Anthropic's early testers: a broker whose wrong-day showing got caught, a restaurant owner who stopped opening 100 tabs, a strategist whose client call clashed with her flight. Honest limits: research preview, US only, Pro and Max, waitlist, it uses your plan's limits, and it can still misjudge what's urgent. The people who get the most out of it already set Claude up properly. That's the part most people skip. #claudeduet #claudecode #learnai #aiagents

Claude Code just got a free way to cut your AI bill. Headroom is an open-source tool with over 77,000 GitHub stars. It shrinks the huge logs, files, and tool outputs your AI coding agent reads before they ever reach the model. In the project's own tests, coding sessions used about 21 to 57 percent fewer tokens, and one 10,000-token log came down to about 1,300 with the important error still in it. Nothing gets deleted, so the AI can still pull up the full original if it needs it. It takes one install and one command, headroom wrap claude, and it works with Codex too. Results depend on what your agent is reading, so check your own savings. Save this for your next coding session. Meta’s Muse is one of the fastest-growing apps of all time... if you go by downloads alone. 10 million US downloads in 40 days puts Muse in the same category as major consumer games like Fortnite and Pokémon Go. But digging into the DAUs tells a deeper story. Only 23% of people were still using Muse two weeks later, and Meta put 39% of its entire October ad budget behind it. That 23% still beats ChatGPT, Claude and Grok, but it only represents about 2.5M DAUs The big test for Meta (and consumer agents generally) will not just be if they can get people to download them, but if those same users will keep coming back day after day.
